title: Tea Nudged Bone Density Up; Five-Plus Coffees a Day Nudged It Down
hook: Ten years of following nearly 10,000 older women found tea drinkers had slightly denser hips — while more than five cups of coffee a day tracked with lower bone density. Moderate coffee looked fine.
key_points: Researchers followed nearly 10,000 older women for 10 years, tracking hip bone density.
Tea drinking was associated with slightly higher hip bone density.
Moderate coffee consumption showed no apparent harm to bone density.
Drinking more than five cups of coffee a day was linked to lower bone density.
This is an observational association in older women — it shows a pattern, not a cause.
content_html: Caffeine's effect on bone has been debated for decades, mostly on the strength of short studies. This one is longer and larger: as ScienceDaily reports, researchers followed nearly 10,000 older women for a decade and tracked hip bone density against their tea and coffee habits.
extra_html:
Two findings came out. Tea drinking was associated with slightly higher hip bone density — a small boost, but a consistent one. Coffee was more conditional: moderate consumption showed no apparent harm, while drinking more than five cups a day was linked to lower bone density.

The usual caveat applies with force here. This is an observational study in older women, so it can identify a pattern but not prove the drink caused it; people who drink five-plus cups of coffee daily may differ in many other ways that also affect bone. The practical reading is undramatic: if you enjoy tea, this is mild good news, and if your coffee habit has crept past five cups, bone density is one more reason to trim it.

related.title: Coffee May Help Your Heart — Energy Drinks, Not So Much
related.hook: A new American Heart Association review says up to ~400 mg of caffeine a day is fine for most hearts, and coffee may even lower some risks. The catch is what you get it from.

related.title: Tea Is Good for You — Until You Add the Wrong Things
related.hook: A major review ties tea to lower risks of heart disease, diabetes, cancer, and cognitive decline — but warns that bottled and bubble teas often pack in ingredients that cancel out the benefits.

related.title: Same BMI, Different Body
related.hook: Finnish researchers found heavier coffee drinkers carried less fat and more muscle than light drinkers at the same BMI — a reminder that the scale hides a lot.

flashcards.prompt: Where did the study find a downside for coffee and bone density?

choices.text: Only above about five cups a day
At any amount of coffee at all
Only in people who also drank tea

flashcards.explanation_html: Moderate coffee consumption did not appear harmful. The association with lower bone density showed up in women drinking more than five cups a day.

flashcards.prompt: Why shouldn't you read this as "tea strengthens bones"?
flashcards.back_html: It's an observational study — nearly 10,000 older women followed for 10 years. It found an association between tea drinking and slightly higher hip bone density, which can't separate the tea from everything else that differs between tea drinkers and non-drinkers.
